plan.question: Full wave64 integer reduction and width32/64 direct-index shuffle across lane and logical-tail boundaries
plan.acceptance: Every physical thread/channel and both guards must pass exact independent CPU checks; retain failures. Reversed order is semantic replication, not a performance treatment.
plan.limitations: One deterministic integer input, complete physical waves and full 64-bit mask only. Timings describe the complete kernel, not intrinsic latency.

input_oracle.value_rule: physical thread i uses input[i] when i < n, else zero; no thread exits before collectives
input_oracle.shuffle_rule: independent width-sized list slices; direct source index wraps within each slice
input_oracle.reduction_rule: exact sum of each independent 64-element wave slice, returned to every thread in that wave
input_oracle.comparison: exact int32 bits for every physical thread and all nine channels, including zeros

artifacts.public_projection: all42cases/420batches; all39744payload+2688guard words read from device outputs; source128words once; device/function/trace resources, rawtrace durations/recompileflags, cachecounts and sanitized allocation/release records

limitations: Full physical wave64 masks only; no sparse-mask, inactive-source, early-exit, partial-physical-wave, down-shuffle, xor or vote claim.
Zero-padding preserves full collective participation; zero-padded threads may receive nonzero values.
Integer correctness for these boundary cases does not prove a native instruction; the installed reduction API may use a software helper.
Descriptive event/host batch timings include complete kernels and possible submission gaps; no intrinsic latency or comparative speedup is reported.
Only final repeated-launch outputs are retained; intermediate invocations were not separately checked.
Register collective observations establish no shared-memory ordering or barrier replacement.
Resource descriptors, cache file counts and recompile flags are observations, not proof of actual residency, physical allocation or compilation counts.
One C550/software stack and deterministic int32 input; no floating-point, arbitrary-mask or target-framework qualification.
